title: The verifier's spoiled-ballot openings under a rolling definition (definition version 7, electorate_mode 2; opening version 3 over ballot version 5's cores, without an author panel): definitions, clocks, boards and pinned panels, with the row 6.2 and the report's openings, beside verifier-ballots-v5.json's group registry events and registration time
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-openings-v3-rolling-vectors.py, from verifier-ballots-v5-vectors.py, ballot-v5-records-vectors.py, verifier-ceremony-vectors.py, spoiled-opening-v3-vectors.py and verifier-openings-v3-vectors.py (independent Python implementations); the ballot records are verifier-ballots-v5.json's

cases.description: A sealed rolling poll without an author panel; close falls in period 2, so s_S is at least 3. Tier 0's ballot (cell 0) in segment 0 (counted whatever s_S is) and tier 2's (cell 1) in segment 4 (counted only if s_S ≥ 4); an honest opening in segment 3 (early); in segment 5 an opening of every check failure (opening-cell for cell 2, the first past a partition of one cell per rolling tier; opening-shape twice, for a missing seat and for an author half the poll has no panel for; opening-ciphertext for seat 2's ciphertext bound to the author panel), one that doesn't decode, one labelled version 2, an honest one, one of three picks in question 1 (outside at question 1), and two that re-use one ballot's (v_j, r_j) under other share hashes: the segment-0 ballot's (cast) and the segment-4 ballot's (undecided); in segment 6 a byte-identical copy of the honest one and of the stray one, and in segment 7 a third copy of the honest one (repeats, each of the first). Each passing opening's tracking code is version 5's core hash. The honest openings above the floor may still be early or late once s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.

Every opening breaks a rule the floor decides: an honest one in segment 3 (early), one re-using the segment-0 ballot's commitment (cast), one failing opening-vss, and a copy of the cast one (repeat). 6.2 fails at the first, opening-early.
The first settled opening is labelled version 2, which a profile pinning version 3 doesn't read: 6.2 fails with decode and profile-mismatch.
Only honest openings above the floor, one per cell, opening no ballot on the copy: undecided until s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.
An opening that re-uses the commitment of tier 2's ballot in segment 4, above the floor: whether that ballot is counted needs s_S, so no break is reported and 6.2 is unverifiable.
The same opening with tier 2's ballot in segment 3, the floor itself: counted whatever s_S is, so the opening is cast and 6.2 fails.
